chapters.title: Chapter 33: The Turning Point of Fate
chapters.content:
Chapter 33: Chapter 33: The Turning Point of Fate
Editor:
Atlas Studios
...
Wang Shouzhe wiped a drop of cold sweat, thinking about those hungry commoners. What would they do to survive when they can’t even buy food with Qian Gold? Sell their children? Sell their houses?
"This means that the more grain the noble families hold in their hands this time, the more they can control the situation. They can make up for their losses through other means and make the family even stronger." Qiaan Xue’an, indeed an excellent businessman, explained the aftermath of this disaster concisely.
"Will the Daqian Government Office and the Purple Mansion Academy transport grains from other counties?" Wang Shouzhe, being a modern Earth person who traveled here, couldn’t bear to see the commoners suffer.
"They will. But the grain needs to be gathered from various counties, then transported and sold at fair prices." Qiaan Xue’an seriously said, "In fact, the Purple Mansion Academy and the Government Office have already started disaster relief today, but it’s nearly impossible to rescue the entire Longzuo County in a short period, especially since our Changning Guard is in a remote location..."
Seeing Wang Shouzhe frowning, he advised, "Younger brother, I know you are kind-hearted. So am I, but with our limited ability, it’s good enough if we manage to take care of ourselves in such times."
"Brother Qian is right. I was being a bit sentimental," Wang Shouzhe acknowledged, "So according to Brother’s suggestion, should I accept triple the contract price from the trading company?"
"You need to understand, younger brother. Even with triple compensation, Qiaan’s Trading Company only breaches the contract as a last resort. No business would want to ruin its reputation." Qiaan Xue’an winked, "Let me give you a number. Insist on ten thousand Qian Gold and grains worth three thousand Qian Gold before agreeing to cancel the contract."
"What?"
Wang Shouzhe’s eye twitched; Qiaan Xue’an was indeed more ruthless than him. Initially, he thought doubling the price to reclaim the contract would already be satisfactory.
This price exceeds the triple compensation, with grains worth an additional three thousand Qian Gold, which is even more valuable.
"You’ve already offended the current shopkeeper of Qiaan’s Trading Company, so might as well go all the way." Qiaan Xue’an chuckled, "Moreover, even at this price, Qiaan’s won’t be at a loss and can still make a profit."
Although Qiaan Xue’an’s reasoning was sound, was it really right to push his own family into such a position?
Seemingly seeing through Wang Shouzhe’s thoughts, Qiaan Xue’an sincerely explained, "Firstly, the Qiaan Family is enormously big, so a mere ten or twenty thousand Qian Gold in compensation is a drop in the ocean. Secondly, I’m just a minor son, and without your help, I’d never climb up the ranks in this life; consider this a small favor in return. Thirdly, I genuinely hope younger brother Shouzhe becomes stronger. Your strength benefits our alliance."
"Alright, let’s do it." With such great benefits, Wang Shouzhe couldn’t refuse. The Wang Race was too poor now, and this sum of money could be a chance for their rise.
"That being the case, let me, Qian, handle this matter for you, younger brother." Qiaan Xue’an seemed to have a plan in mind, "I’ll report to the shopkeeper, deliberately raising the price by another 30%, then negotiate a discount to give him some comfort. Additionally, younger brother Shouzhe, you must swear not to spread this around; Qiaan’s Trading Company can’t afford such a loss of face."
Naturally, keeping quiet and reaping the rewards in silence is the best option.
Wang Shouzhe stood up and cupped his hands, "In that case, I’ll leave it to you, Brother. One more condition: the Insecticide Powder must not be sold to the Ping’an Zhao Family and the Ping’an Liu Family." For Wang Shouzhe, strengthening oneself was good, but weakening the enemy was even better.
"Even without this condition, I would have considered it," Qiaan Xue’an replied with a smile, "Moreover, during this disaster, the demand for Insecticide Powder vastly outstrips the supply. The Ping’an Zhao Family and the Ping’an Liu Family are just lower-rank noble families and it’s already extremely difficult for them to secure a share of the Insecticide Powder. Congratulations, younger brother!"
In the Ping’an Wang Family’s eyes, the Liu Family and the Zhao Family were formidable adversaries, but in Qiaan’s Trading Company’s eyes, they were just two ordinary small clans.
"Congratulations to you too."
Both of them laughed as their negotiation was concluded.
Immediately, Qiaan Xue’an smashed his cup to the ground, roaring as he left: "Wang Shouzhe, you’ve gone too far, do you think our Qiaan’s Trading Company is to be trifled with? Just wait and see..."
He then stormed off, with the two frightened guards outside following him.
Wang Shouzhe was quite satisfied with Qiaan Xue’an’s reaction and tactics. It seemed he hadn’t chosen the wrong ally.
Just then, his second elder brother Wang Shouyi walked in anxiously, "Shouzhe, that Steward Qiaan has come looking for you several times these past two days. Has something happened?"
The present Wang Race couldn’t withstand much turbulence.
"Don’t worry, second brother. It’s good for the family," Wang Shouzhe replied with a smile, then changed the subject, "By the way, how’s the research on live fish equipment going these past two days?"
At the mention of this, Wang Shouyi brightened up, "I must say, Shouzhe, your idea is unique and brilliant. The methods of spraying to increase oxygen and changing water with a suction pump alone can transform the whole aquaculture storage and transportation industry. I’ve tested it initially, and the effects are excellent. Next, we need to modify the water buckets in the carriages and the ponds in the shop."
"So, second brother, you must speed up the progress and build more ponds in the backyard," Wang Shouzhe laughed, "Otherwise, Uncle Six will come to scold you."
"That’s right. Uncle Six has more and more live fish these two days..." Wang Shouyi cupped his hands, "Fourth brother, I must take my leave now." Then he hurriedly ran out.
Haha, Wang Shouyi’s initiative had indeed increased, which was a good thing. No wonder, the family’s improving prospects boosted the clan’s morale.
Wang Shouzhe placed great importance on the fishing team and fish market, two clan industries. Previously, these two ventures combined brought in a net profit of just four to five hundred Qian Gold annually. However, with his suggestions and adjustments, net profits exceeding a thousand were easily achievable.
He was even confident that by the following year, the fishing team and fish market’s profits would surpass those of the three big farms combined.
Profiting greatly from speculating on Insecticide Powder was something worth celebrating. However, the development of the clan industry was the true foundation of a family’s strength.
Additionally, the stockpile of grains worth three thousand Qian Gold mentioned by Qiaan Xue’an gave Wang Shouzhe a bit of a headache. In a year of disaster, holding grain meant holding the advantage, no doubt about that.
But what kind of concept is three thousand Qian Gold in grain? Given current grain prices, that’s enough to feed two million people for a year!
Bear in mind, the total population of Ping’an Town was less than thirty thousand.
Such a massive quantity of grain presented significant challenges in terms of transportation and storage. Naturally, the major farms of the Ping’an Wang Family were equipped with granaries, but they were already nearly full with last year’s old grain and this year’s harvest. At most, they could squeeze in another ten to twenty thousand Du.
But solutions are always created by people.
When Ancestor Zhou Xuan established the main residence, he considered the family’s future development. He built fifty courtyards for important clan members and, all told, the house included hundreds of rooms.
The majority of them were empty, and with some tidying up, storing tens of thousands of Du of grain was easy. In a disaster year, the safest place was the noble family’s main residence.
Each noble family’s main residence was built on terrain that was easy to defend and difficult to attack, with the strongest defensive forces. Storing grain there put everyone at ease.
Earlier it was mentioned that Wang’s main residence was built by the mountains and beside a lake.
The mountain was part of Liping Mountain’s outlying ranges, and the lake was a small body of water called Zhuwei Lake. This lake was named personally by Ancestor Zhou Xuan after his most beloved daughter Wang Zhuwei, using her maiden name.
Zhuwei Lake wasn’t large, covering barely ten thousand acres of water, but it was the natural shield and back garden of Wang’s main residence.
Most importantly, it had a natural river route later improved by human hands. This river, a few miles forward, branched off to connect, besides the Silkworm Manor, the other two major farms.
Fenggu Farm’s main river connects meanderingly with Zhuwei Lake, a total distance of over twenty miles.
And upstream of Fenggu Farm’s river is the sluice gate Ancestor Zhou Xuan built back then, called Fenggu Gate. This gate is a hydraulic structure mainly used to regulate the water level of the inner river channels, but because it used a winch-style single gate, ships can’t pass through.
However, this didn’t matter much, as inside and outside Fenggu Gate, regular dredging and maintenance kept the waterway open, so the water level was deep enough...
Wang Shouzhe quickly organized his thoughts and, after writing two letters, called in Wang Zhong and Wang Yong.
"Patriarch," both Household Generals appeared energetic and in high spirits, clearly optimistic about the family’s future development.
Wang Shouzhe handed over the letters to Household Generals Wang Zhong and Wang Yong to deliver, instructing, "After delivering the letters, don’t return immediately; stay there to help."
After the Household Generals left with orders, Wang Shouzhe sat sipping tea alone, the stormy look in his eyes revealing his inner turmoil. If everything went smoothly, this insect disaster might turn out to be a turning point for the Wang Race’s declining fate.
...

chapters.title: Chapter 34: Pulling One Hair Affects the Entire Body
chapters.content:
Chapter 34: Chapter 34: Pulling One Hair Affects the Entire Body
Editor:
Atlas Studios
...
Time passed uneventfully for two days.
During these two days, Young Clan Leader Wang Shouzhe stayed at the Changning Villa, cultivating his mind and body, sipping spirit tea, cultivating, living a rather leisurely life.
However, in the outside world, things drastically changed over these two days. As wheat matured rapidly, the first wave of insect plagues struck with unexpected swiftness, spreading across the entire Changning Guard Region, throwing all the noble families into disarray.
With reduced production inevitable, the prices of agricultural and sideline products, except for the staple grains strictly controlled by the Daqian Government Office, began to rise. Even Wang’s Fish Stall’s business in salted fish and smoked fish suddenly improved significantly, with prices also seeing a substantial increase. In the absence of staple grains, preserved salted and smoked fish became a means to sustain life.
All trading companies and rice stores have ceased selling grains externally. As for the rice stores managed by the Daqian Government, they began limiting sales, with long queues forming in front, and the City Guard intervening to maintain order.
While sipping tea and listening to the aggregated news from various sources, Wang Shouzhe’s heart was unsettled. If not for the family having a gem like Wang Luojing, they probably would have been in dire straits by now, wouldn’t they?
How could one be as leisurely and carefree as now, observing the storm gather?
"Fourth Brother, Qiaan’s Trading Company sent a letter," Wang Shouyi personally came to the backyard to deliver the letter, his brow furrowed. "Besides, the salted and smoked fish inventory that Sixth Uncle sent has already sold half in these past two days. I noticed other families’ fish stalls have started to limit purchases or significantly raise prices. Should our fish stall also raise prices?"
Even salted fish need to be limited in sales?
After taking the letter, Wang Shouzhe frowned. It seems the news of a large-scale reduction in grain production has already sparked panic. This scene is not unfamiliar to him; during his time on Earth, he saw numerous instances of ordinary people rushing to buy goods during disasters or rumors, collectively panicking.
Moreover, the salted and smoked fish were sold too quickly, weren’t they? The inventory gradually delivered over several times amounted to about eight or nine hundred bundles. Before the price hike, salted and smoked fish varied in price from 20 to 30 coins per pound, and a bundle usually ranged from 20 large coppers to 30 large coppers.
Now the price has risen to 30 to 40 large coppers per bundle, yet it’s selling even faster.
"What about live and fresh fish?" Wang Shouzhe asked.
"The price for live fish hasn’t increased, but fresh fish generally saw a 20% rise," Wang Shouyi reported. "Many people bought fresh fish to marinate or smoke themselves, or to reduce staple loss by consuming more fish, so salt and firewood also rose in price."
Indeed, a slight change can affect everything.
The outbreak of resistant aphids instantly impacted various aspects. Once basic materials like salt, firewood, and coal increase in price, everything else follows suit.
"Second Brother, just increase prices according to the market," Wang Shouzhe said. "As for limiting sales, announce a restriction of twenty bundles per day for salted and smoked fish externally, while internally sell up to fifty bundles."
"Fifty bundles? That’s a full five thousand pounds..." Wang Shouyi exclaimed, "Can Sixth Uncle keep up? Even if Sixth Uncle can, the Dingpu Warehouse can’t keep up with processing and marinating."
It’s the abundant fishing season now. If Wang Dinghai’s fishing team operates like past years, ten ships working hard can catch thousands of pounds easily, with each fishing boat averaging only a few hundred pounds of common catch.
Most of them would be marinated or smoked in the Dingpu Warehouse. Under normal circumstances, the drying and smoking fish workshop there can reach up to 800 bundles a month at most.
However, Wang Dinghai has already fully replicated fixed processing equipment, which even ordinary people can operate. During this abundant fishing season, the entire fishing team producing over ten thousand pounds isn’t unusual.
"Increase the manpower and space for fish processing, utilize vacant spaces and rooms at Fenggu Farm and Xingsheng Farm. Also, have all household servants and idle family members participate to guarantee a production of over two thousand bundles of smoked and salted fish this month," Wang Shouzhe instructed, "Second Brother, you fully oversee this task."
"As long as Sixth Uncle can keep up, I’m not afraid." In that instant, Wang Shouyi was also fueled with enthusiasm—a monthly production of two thousand bundles of smoked and salted fish requires at least three to four thousand bundles of fresh fish, as the weight significantly reduces after slaughtering, smoking, and drying.
If Sixth Uncle could truly meet the production needs, this is a prime opportunity to profit. How could Wang Shouyi lag behind?
In previous years, the bounty from the fishing season was the cheapest, so a large quantity of common catches would be made into smoked and salted fish to be sold gradually. The total annual production and sales of smoked and salted fish were only two thousand plus bundles in the past. In terms of fresh and live fish, the total annual sales were only two thousand bundles or so.
Overall business revenue struggled to surpass one thousand Qian Gold, of which roughly half had to be allocated to the fishing team’s account.
But things are different now.
If this month they could produce over two thousand bundles, selling fifteen hundred bundles of smoked and pickled fish at a raised price of forty large coppers per bundle, the revenue would reach six hundred Qian Gold.
This doesn’t even include the sales of fresh and live fish... this month’s revenue might potentially reach that of an entire normal year.
That’s why Wang Shouyi felt his blood boiling! If not now, then when?
"Alright, then I’ll have to trouble Second Brother to handle things on both sides." Wang Shouzhe wrote a clan leader’s order, signed it, stamped it with the Clan Leader’s Seal, and handed it to him, saying, "With this, you can mobilize household generals and household servants and draw Qian Gold from the family treasury."
"I don’t need Qian Gold for now." Wang Shouyi took the letter of mandate, excited, "This time the inventory of salted fish sold too fast. I still have a couple of hundred Qian Gold on hand, enough to operate."
"Second Brother, while busy, be sure not to make mistakes or overlook anything in the accounts," Wang Shouzhe casually warned.
Wang Shouyi was taken aback, his expression turned serious, and he hurriedly said, "Rest assured Fourth Brother, as a member of the family, I would never violate clan rules. I hand over the accounts with Aunt Five overseeing the treasury every month, daring not to overlook anything."
"Thank you, Second Brother." Wang Shouzhe solemnly bowed to him, "Such a rare opportunity, whether the Wang Family can escape decline, requires the entire family to exert their utmost efforts."
Wang Shouzhe was quite satisfied; although his Second Brother’s cultivation talent was mediocre, he was very dedicated to the family business. Compared with Sixth Uncle Wang Dinghai, who was a rough man, he was much more meticulous and steady.
"Fourth Brother, you’re too kind, this is my duty." Wang Shouyi hurriedly bowed back, saying, "In this case, I’ll take my leave to handle various affairs."
After he left, Wang Shouzhe composed himself and opened the letter from Qiaan Xue’an, inviting him to meet outside Changning Guard City at [Money Manor]. Through the secret marks left in the letter, Qiaan Xue’an indicated he had fulfilled their agreement.
Though he trusted Qiaan Xue’an, he dared not take risks this time, opting for safety first in all matters.
Decisively, he dressed up a bit, left the city directly, and instead of heading to Money Manor, he rode a black horse towards Shanyang. After a short while, he arrived outside a small estate a few miles from the city and met Wang Zhong.
"Wang Zhong, how did it go?" Wang Shouzhe asked.
"The preparation went well, Young Master," Wang Zhong responded, slightly excited, as he had been waiting outside the estate for over seven to eight hours.
Considering that the Wang Family’s influence south of the Anjiang River wasn’t strong, they had to rely on the Shanyang Gongsun Family to secure a large number of cargo wagons. Their relationship with the Gongsun Family was in a honeymoon phase, so such a small request wouldn’t be rejected.
Meeting with Gongsun Qiang at the small villa outside the city, he clasped his hands and said, "Shouzhe greets you, Uncle-in-law, apologies for keeping you waiting."
"Shouzhe, my dear nephew," Gongsun Qiang, being straightforward and impatient, blurted out with curiosity, "You say you mysteriously asked for heavily laden wagons from me, twenty in all, for transporting ores? What is going on?"
"Just over fifty to sixty thousand bundles of grain, that’s all." Since involving him would inevitably reveal the quantity, there was no point in hiding it.
"..."
At that moment, Gongsun Qiang felt his eyes nearly popping out in shock, "Dear Nephew, you do realize that right now grain is scarce as any bundle is hard to come by? And here you are with fifty to sixty thousand bundles..."
Just, that’s all?
He felt as if he’d lost his mind to even think badly of himself in comparison to his "clever nephew."
